sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Northampton County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
The county divides the job in two. The Assessment Office sets and maintains the value of every parcel, while the Revenue and Tax Claim Office bills, collects and chases unpaid taxes. Both sit in the government center at 669 Washington Street in Easton.

Assessment is in Room 2112 on the second floor, phone 610-829-6155. Revenue and Tax Claim answers at 610-829-6186. A third body, the Revenue Appeals Board, hears assessment disputes.

The county has run under a home rule charter since 1978, with an elected executive and a council, and appeal fees are set by council resolution. A seller in Northampton County usually needs two items from these offices: the parcel's current assessment and a tax certification showing what is owed.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Northampton County assessment?
sections.html:
File with the Revenue Appeals Board by August 1. An annual appeal filed by that date earns a hearing, and any change applies to the following tax year.

Northampton County assessment appeal rules, procedures revised June 15, 2026
ItemRule
Annual appeal deadlineAugust 1
Interim appeal (notice of change)40 days from the notice date
Residential filing fee$25 per parcel
Commercial or exemption filing fee$250 per parcel
Hearing noticeAt least 20 days before the hearing
Supporting documents due10 business days before the hearing
Appeal of a board decision to court30 days from the mailing date

Source: the Revenue Appeals Board procedures posted by the county. Each parcel needs its own application, signed by the record owner whose name is on the deed, and the filing fee is not refunded.

  • Residential forms must list the most recent comparable sales. Without them the assessment may stay as it is.
  • A residential property assessed at $175,000 or more needs an appraisal by a state certified appraiser.
  • Restricted appraisal reports are not accepted.
  • Filing can raise the assessment as well as lower it, a risk the board warns about.

sections.h2: Has the 2026 appeal season ended in Northampton County?
sections.html:
August 1, 2026 has come and gone, and the board's posted hearing dates ran from August 5 through October 29. An owner who missed it waits for the next August 1, unless the county mails a notice of change, which opens a 40-day interim window.

The board also reschedules a hearing once, for a $25 fee. An appellant who does not show up is treated as having abandoned the appeal and loses the right to go on to the Court of Common Pleas. The county posts the Common Level Ratio each July 1, and a seller deciding whether an appeal is worth the effort should ask the Assessment Office for the current figure and the parcel's recent comparable sales.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exclusion work in Northampton County?
sections.html:
It trims the assessed value on which school property tax is computed for a primary residence. Under Act 72 of 2004, school districts draw on state gaming revenue and local income taxes to give every approved homestead the same dollar reduction before the tax is figured.

  • Applications go to the county Assessment Office and are due by March 1.
  • The exclusion applies to one primary residence, so a second home does not qualify.
  • Owners must report a change in use within 45 days, such as turning the house into a rental.
  • A denied application can be appealed within 40 days of the date on the letter.
  • A false application brings back taxes, interest, a 10 percent penalty and possible misdemeanor charges.

Some school boards choose not to adopt the exclusion, so ask your school district what applies. A seller moving out should tell the assessor, since a house that stops being a homestead should not keep the exclusion.

sections.h2: How and where do I pay Northampton County property tax?
sections.html:
The county runs an online portal for current taxes, and its payment page announces that the 2026 real estate tax portal is live. That page lists fees of 3.5 percent for credit cards and $4 for electronic checks under $29,999.

Past-due accounts are handled by phone at 610-829-6186. The county has said it anticipates a separate way to pay balances less than two years behind that are not subject to sale, so ask the Revenue Office which option fits your parcel.

The same page links the tax certification that a closing agent requests. Closing agents commonly ask for it, so order it early instead of waiting for the final week before the closing date.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes in Northampton County?
sections.html:
They go to the Tax Claim Bureau and can end up at a sale. The county posted a Judicial Sale for May 27, 2026 and an Upset Sale for September 24, 2026, both at 1:00 p.m. in Courtroom 1, and both dates are behind us. The upset sale falls in September each year.

State law adopted in House Bill 264 of 2021 requires bidders to register before any tax sale. For the 2026 upset sale, registration ran from August 31 through September 14 and was available only at the courthouse government center in Easton, with no exceptions.

An owner with a lapsed bill should contact the Revenue Office well before September. Ask the Tax Claim Office what clearing the account would take before a sale date. A seller who is behind should tell the title agent at the start.

sections.h2: How can I look up my assessment before listing a house?
sections.html:
The Assessment Office links a public site, ncpub.org, where county assessment data can be reviewed online. Search by address or parcel, then compare the assessed value with recent sales of similar houses on your street.

  • Note the tax map identification: district, map, block and lot. Appeals and the homestead form both ask for it.
  • Check the school district and municipality listed for the parcel, because the homestead application asks for both.
  • Look at the building details, such as rooms, baths, garage and lot size, and report any error to the office.
  • Confirm whether a homestead exclusion is already applied before you sell.

Buyers ask what the tax bill looks like, so having the parcel record ready saves a round of questions. The Assessment Office also offers a change of address form for a tax bill that still goes to an old address.

sections.h2: What is the Northampton County housing picture for sellers?
sections.html:
This Lehigh Valley county spans 377 square miles. Easton is the seat, Bethlehem is the largest city, and the Delaware River marks the eastern border with New Jersey. The county dates to 1752 and long led in steel and cement.

The federal estimate for 2025 is 324,411 residents, up 3.7 percent on the 2020 base. The latest five-year survey puts the median owned home at $308,600, median household income at $89,184 and median gross rent at $1,395. Cities, boroughs and townships all sit inside the same county assessment system, so the parcel record is a better guide to your own tax bill than any county average.

faqs.q: What is the last day to challenge an assessment in Northampton County?
faqs.a: August 1. A yearly appeal reaches the Revenue Appeals Board only if it is filed by then, and any result applies to the next tax year. Interim appeals get 40 days from a notice of change.

faqs.q: What does it cost to file an assessment appeal in Northampton County?
faqs.a: $25 per parcel for a residential appeal and $250 for a commercial or exemption appeal. The money is not refunded, and moving a hearing costs another $25.

faqs.q: Does an appeal in Northampton County require an appraisal?
faqs.a: Yes, once the residential assessed value reaches $175,000. A state certified appraiser must prepare it, and restricted reports are refused.

faqs.q: By when must a Northampton County owner request the homestead exclusion?
faqs.a: By March 1, filed with the county Assessment Office, which sends a written notice if the request is denied.

faqs.q: How long do I have to take a board decision to court in Northampton County?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the mailing date of the board's notice, filed in the Court of Common Pleas. An appellant who abandoned the hearing gives up that right.
